events.credibility_reason: Claimed landmark nonexistence proof with no journal publication or uptake in about 7 years; Wikipedia, Epoch, Ishida (2026) and Smith-Montemanni (2026) all still call the problem open; arXiv identity of the paper itself is confused.

Faber and Keegan (2022) identify a specific flaw in the key case analysis (the equation system splits into small diagonal blocks that all have solutions); no answer found, never published, and later work treats the problem as open.

events.ai_basis: using a construction discovered through interaction with ChatGPT via its standard web interface

why: The statement asks only whether the degree-57 Moore graph exists. Structural constraints on a hypothetical graph (automorphism bounds, critical group, adjacency constraints, partial t-subgraphs) settle no restriction of the existence question and are scored none; the 2026 cyclic-derangement result rules out a construction method, not a class of graphs, so it is none (F4). The close call is Ishida (2026): proving no such graph has an involutory automorphism settles nonexistence within a class of objects (graphs with even-order automorphism group), which I score as case, in the same way as the pre-snapshot vertex-transitivity/rank-3 exclusions; direction is left null because the statement is a question, not a conjecture with an expected answer. Makhnev's 2020 nonexistence claim carries a specific, unanswered objection to its key case analysis and is knocked down; Yang-Zhu has no uptake for seven years while every later source calls the problem open, so not credible. Mizuno is a different problem (degree/diameter at diameter 5) and Bandeira et al. a hypergraph analogue: variants. Mizuno's ChatGPT construction is generated for that event only; the Bandeira AI lead is unverified and has no systems entry, so none. Journal publications are scored digested as journals of record. The Epoch listing's year-only 2026 date cannot be placed against 26 January.
doubts: Ishida's case scope is a judgement call: a reader could treat 'no involutions' as a structural constraint (none) rather than a settled class. Ishida is unreviewed, single-author, from an outfit named 'A.I. System Research, Inc.'; the final 69 HTML characters (possibly acknowledgements) were not read, so an AI disclosure cannot be ruled out. Smith-Montemanni 2024/2026 details rest on search summaries (pages 403).
